There is a higher level of uncertainty with this analysis due to limited triangulation ability as well as the unique shape of the CME front. This analysis tracks the furthest out portion of the shock (the "nose") of the CME and includes most of the shock that is more in the ecliptic plane, however this measurement also includes unavoidable empty/dead space due to the overall shape of the shock front and the restrictions of the SWPC_CAT measuring tool.

data.note: CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-05-24T20:00Z. It is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3, but is obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. The source is most likely related to some field line movement seen beyond the NE limb best seen in GOES SUVI 284 beginning as early as 2026-05-24T18:30Z. The field line movement can also be faintly seen well beyond the E limb in STEREO A EUVI 195. There is also a narrow feature to the E in STEREO A COR2 that could be this CME, but a good triangulated fit cannot be made between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, particularly due to the grainy image quality in COR2A. No additional source was found.

data.note: Faint CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and to the N/NW in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source of this CME is a filament eruption visible beyond the NE limb in GOES SUVI 304 and 284 starting around 2026-05-25T06:57Z. This eruption is also visible in SDO/AIA wavelengths.

data.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. This event is not seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery due to a data gap starting at 2026-05-25T20:53Z. Additionally, this event is blocked by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is a far-sided eruption visible over the northeast limb in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 imagery starting around 2026-05-25T20:09Z. A faint opening of field lines is observed over the northwest limb in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195 imagery.

data.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This event is not seen STEREO A COR2 imagery due to the data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery starting at 2026-05-25T20:53Z. The source is an eruption visible near the northeast limb in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery starting around 2026-05-26T21:12Z. A subsequent opening of field lines is observed over the northeast limb in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 imagery.

data.note: Fast, halo CME first seen to the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-05-25T22:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is likely a far sided flare seen by the Solar orbiter STIX instrument peaking at approx. 2026-05-25T22:04Z with an estimated peak of M7.3 (potential range of [M4.0,X1.4]). Filament ejecta can also be seen in association with this eruption beyond the NW limb in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304 beginning at approx. 2026-05-25T21:57Z, along with wide opening field lines and EUV wave observed in SDO AIA 171, 193 and GOES SUVI 284. This event is also associated with solar energetic particle enhancements at SOHO, GOES and STEREO Ahead.

Preliminary leading edge analysis, assuming former AR 14436 (~N18W145 at this time). STEREO A COR2 observations not available due to data gap, and not yet observed in LASCO C3.

Shock front analysis with SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. STEREO A COR2 not available due to a data gap. The shock front is notably irregular shaped, with a northern lobe and southern feature observed as a wide partial halo. This fit tracks the majority of the observed shock front prioritizing the northern lobe in similarity to the bulk leading edge directionality. Longitude of W145 used as the approximate source of former AR 14436; the likely source for this CME without direct observation, and as such longitude could vary between W135-W155.

A subsequent opening of field lines is visible over the northeast limb in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/193/284 imagery.

A second filament ejecta follows immediately after directed further northward, responsible for separate overlapping CME: 2026-05-26T21:36Z.
